question.text: Scenario: Mrs. Anita is 62 years old and has just retired from a private sector company with a total retirement corpus of Rs. 2,00,00,000 (Rs. 2 crore). She owns a house and has no outstanding loans. Her monthly household expenses are Rs. 80,000. She wants to generate a steady monthly income while preserving her capital for at least 25 years. She is considering multiple distribution options: annuities from an insurance company, SWP from mutual funds, SCSS, POMIS, FD laddering, and possibly a reverse mortgage on her property (valued at Rs. 1.5 crore). She has no other source of income. Her husband (age 65) is also retired. She wants to allocate her Rs. 2 crore optimally across these products. Question 2 of 5: Mrs. Anita is comparing annuity options for Rs. 50,00,000 of her corpus. She has two specific requirements: (i) her husband must continue to receive annuity income after her death, and (ii) the purchase price must be returned to their children at the end. Among the four options below, which option best satisfies BOTH requirements (income continuation to the spouse AND return of purchase price)?

answer.text: Lifetime annuity without return of purchase price — covers only her life and does not return capital
Annuity certain for 25 years — fixed-term payments only, neither survivorship nor capital return
Joint life annuity with return of purchase price — covers both lives and returns capital to nominees
Lifetime annuity with return of purchase price for single life — covers only her life but returns capital

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series X-B workbook pp. 108-109 explain joint annuities (which continue paying to the surviving spouse) and return-of-purchase-price annuities (which return the capital to the nominee at the end) as separate features. Mrs. Anita's two requirements line up exactly with these two features: only an option that combines both — a joint life annuity with return of purchase price — satisfies survivorship AND capital return. Option C is therefore uniquely correct. The Trap: Option A fails the capital-return requirement. Option B fails both requirements (fixed-term, not life-contingent, and no capital return). Option D fails the survivorship requirement (covers only Mrs. Anita's life, not her husband). The audit flagged the original explanation for asserting that the joint-life-with-return-of-purchase-price option has "the lowest annuity rate among all options" — a rate-ranking claim the workbook pages checked do not explicitly support. That ranking has been removed. Note: The original option C made an unsourced rate-ranking claim ("lowest annuity rate among all options"). The stem and options have been reframed around the two features that ARE separately supported by NISM Series X-B pp. 108-109 (joint life and return of purchase price), so option C is now uniquely correct on the feature criterion alone, without relying on the rate-ranking claim.
